s1loc: Exmouth Food Bank supports people across the town and surrounding villages of Lympstone, Woodbury and Budleigh Salterton, run entirely by volunteers. Open Door Exmouth, a multi-service charity at the heart of the community since 1995, runs a Community Cafe, a Community Fridge, a clothing store and showers, tackling isolation and poverty. The Salvation Army food bank and Exmouth Friends in Need, founded in 2018 to alleviate family poverty, add to a busy local scene of small volunteer-run projects.

The sector here runs at every size. National charities such as Age UK and the big food-redistribution and foodbank networks keep shops on the high street and buy kit centrally, while Exeter Food Action with FareShare South West moves surplus to community groups across East Devon. Alongside them, small community fridges, pantries and volunteer-run foodbanks work on a shoestring across The Strand, Littleham and Withycombe Raleigh. We are set up to serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts and direct online ordering, no minimum.

Beyond food support, Exmouth backs a wide spread of further good causes. Hospiscare, the Exeter-based hospice, runs a charity shop in the town and depends on volunteers, while Open Door, the British Heart Foundation and other shops line Rolle Street and the town centre. Mutual-aid and befriending groups, the Exmouth in Bloom volunteers and community wellbeing projects all draw on local people giving their time. The result is a dense network of named charities and tiny shoestring projects sitting side by side across Exmouth.

s1loc: Footprints in the Community, led by Ruth Fox MBE, runs a network of foodbank centres and support projects across Redcar and Cleveland, while the Redcar Area Foodbank gives out emergency parcels with volunteers collecting donations outside Asda South Bank. TEES, a registered charity formed in 2019, hands out food parcels across the Tees Valley with unpaid trustees, and East Cleveland Good Neighbours runs a community-led food bank for the rural villages. Together they form a busy grassroots food network.

Mutual-aid networks, befriending schemes and the volunteer-driven good-neighbour projects of East Cleveland all sit alongside the foodbanks. From named hospice shops to one-room neighbourhood projects, the spread of causes across Redcar relies on local people giving their time week in, week out.

whitley bay.s1_head: Charity and volunteers in Whitley Bay
s1loc: The Bay Foodbank, started in 2012 with help from local churches in Whitley Bay, now works from a warehouse with extra storage in North Shields and gives out around 40 emergency parcels a day across North Tyneside. Age UK North Tyneside supports older people and their carers across the borough, while VODA, the North Tyneside volunteer development agency, helps charities and community groups grow. St Oswald's Hospice draws gardening and shop volunteers from the town, anchoring a busy local scene.

The sector here runs at every size. Whitley Bay's voluntary life runs deep. Whitley Bay Big Local, an independent community charity since 2017, works to reduce loneliness and financial exclusion, while the Repair Cafe volunteers at St Mary's Church in Monkseaton and the Friends of St Mary's Island give their time to the wider area. Scout groups, befriending schemes and seafront community projects add to the mix, supported by VODA. From named hospice and charity shops to tiny volunteer-run groups, the spread of causes across Whitley Bay depends on local people giving freely.

houghton le spring.s1_head: Charity and volunteers in Houghton le Spring
s1loc: Space 4 Food Bank and Community Store on Newbottle Street in Houghton le Spring gives out emergency parcels and runs an affordable community food store two days a week for a small suggested donation. It sits within the wider Sunderland Foodbank network, part of the Trussell Trust, which now has ten foodbanks across the city working on a voucher referral system. A new Sunderland Foodbank centre opened in Houghton with support from Gentoo and Esh Construction, strengthening local food support.

Houghton le Spring's wider charity scene runs on volunteers too. St Benedict's Hospice in Sunderland has given free palliative care for over 35 years and depends on volunteers across its care teams and shops, while the Penshaw Community Association on Wensleydale Avenue runs community activities for local people. Mutual-aid groups, befriending schemes and community associations across Hetton and Shiney Row all draw on neighbours giving their time. From the named hospice to the one-room food store, the spread of causes here relies on grassroots effort.

s1loc: Warwick District Foodbank, part of the Trussell Trust network and a registered charity since 2015, gives emergency food and support to people in crisis across Warwick, Leamington and Kenilworth, distributing more than 37,000 parcels between 2021 and 2025. Formed when two local foodbanks merged in 2017, it is powered by volunteers, faith groups, schools, businesses and residents, with Warwickshire Community and Voluntary Action helping coordinate local volunteering. It anchors a busy grassroots food-support scene for the district.

Warwick's charity life leans heavily on its hospice movement. Community groups, befriending schemes and mutual-aid projects support residents across the district, while charity shops line the town and Leamington nearby. From the named hospice shops to one-room volunteer foodbanks, the spread of causes across Warwick depends on local people giving their time.
